  original token is rejected (anti-takeover). If a provider durably lost its
  token, delete the router's registry state (state scope `llm-router`,
  key `registry`) and restart the affected providers to re-bind; pasted
  credentials in the configuration entry are unaffected.

## Security model

The agent-callable surface is governed by the engine-wide permission policy
(repo-root [`iii-permissions.yaml`](https://github.com/iii-hq/workers/blob/main/iii-permissions.yaml)), not a per-worker
file. In-run agents may only **read** the catalog and provider list:

- **Allowed:** `router::models::list`, `router::models::get`,
  `router::models::supports`, `router::provider::list`.
- **Denied to agents:** the chat/spend surface (`router::chat`,
  `router::complete`, `router::abort`, `router::route`), the whole
  provider/credential protocol (`router::provider::resolve` / `register` /
  `update_credential`, `router::models::reconcile`), and direct `provider::*`
  calls.

Worker-to-worker calls bypass the agent gate, so the harness, context-manager,
and provider workers reach the full surface — only in-run agents are
restricted. Provider credentials live in the configuration entry, or behind a
`secret://` or `env://` reference in the `secrets` worker, and are never readable back
through any allowed function: `router::provider::list` reports where a
credential comes from, never its value.

## Events

The router registers three custom trigger types and fans out to every bound
handler. Bind with the standard two-step pattern; the handler receives the
payload verbatim (no envelope).

| Trigger type | Fires when | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| `router::models::changed` | a provider reconciles its catalog slice | `{ "provider": "<id>", "count": <n> }` |
| `router::provider::changed` | the registry changes (declare / availability flip) | `{ "provider": "<id>", "op": "register" \| "available" \| "unavailable" }` |
| `router::ready` | the router finishes booting; providers re-declare on it | `{}` |

The router itself binds the engine's `configuration` trigger (its entry) and,
when the optional `secrets` worker is installed, `secrets::changed`
(`router::on_secret_changed`).

```ts
iii.registerFunction('my-worker::on-models-changed', async (payload) => {
  console.log('catalog changed:', payload); // { provider, count }
  return {};
});

iii.registerTrigger({
  type: 'router::models::changed',
  function_id: 'my-worker::on-models-changed',
  config: {},
});
```

## Writing a provider worker

A provider worker must:

1. Register `provider::<id>::stream` honouring the channel-writer contract:
   forward upstream output as `AssistantMessageEvent` frames into the
   `writer_ref` it receives, ending with one terminal frame.
2. Declare itself at startup via `router::provider::register` — retrying with
   backoff until acknowledged (covers provider-before-router boot order) —
   and re-declare on the `router::ready` event after a router restart. The
   declaration may carry `icon_svg`: one self-contained, monochrome `<svg>`
   document (square `viewBox`, no fixed size, at most 32 KiB). The router
   echoes it in `router::provider::list` and the console paints it as a
   `currentColor` mask beside the provider's models; a missing or malformed
   mark falls back to the provider's initial.
   The declaration may also carry `default_models`, the provider's
   recommended starting models in preference order (the current mid-range
   model first, then its predecessors), and `default_thinking_level`, the
   level to pair with it; see [Default model](#default-model).
3. Resolve credentials per request via `router::provider::resolve`; never
   read keys directly. A response with `credential_source: "secret"` and no
   credential is an unresolvable `secret://` or `env://` reference: report its
   `credential_error`, do not substitute a key of your own.
4. Treat closure of its stream channel as cancellation: abort the upstream
   request and stop writing frames.
5. Map upstream failures to the shared `ErrorKind` taxonomy on its `error`
   frames. Transport retries (429 / 5xx / connect) are the router's job, not
   the provider's.

A provider may also register `provider::<id>::count_tokens` (`{model,
system_prompt?, tools?, messages, thinking_level?, response_format?}` →
`{model, tokens, estimator}`; the last two are the turn's `router::chat`
values, sent only when set) to serve
`router::count_tokens`: an exact count from a provider metering API
(`estimator: "provider"`) or a local tokenizer estimate (`estimator:
"tiktoken"`). Providers without it simply make `router::count_tokens` return
a typed `router/no_token_counter` error for that provider.

content.content:
# Agent permissions for the provider-deepseek worker.
# Spec: tech-specs/2026-06-agentic/llm-router.md § Security.
version: 1

rules:
  # Direct provider calls bypass the router's accounting, budgets, and retry
  # policy — never agent-callable. The router invokes these worker-to-worker.
  - '!provider::deepseek::stream'
  - '!provider::deepseek::refresh_models'
  - '!provider::deepseek::on_router_ready'
  - '!provider::deepseek::count_tokens'
iii: v1
name: provider-deepseek
language: rust
deploy: binary
manifest: Cargo.toml
license: Apache-2.0
bin: provider-deepseek
tags: [llm, deepseek, chat-completions, provider]
description: DeepSeek Chat Completions provider worker; implements provider::deepseek::stream and provider::deepseek::refresh_models behind llm-router.

dependencies:
  state: "latest"
  llm-router: "latest"
# provider-deepseek has no file-based configuration.
#
# Credentials, `api_url`, and `max_tokens` arrive per request from
# llm-router's resolve step; the provider block lives in the engine's
# `llm-router` configuration entry (README § Configuration).
#
# This file exists to satisfy the standard worker layout
# (docs/sops/new-worker.md §2). Keys placed here are ignored with a warning.
85:  llm-router:
86:    worker: package://llm-router
88:  provider-anthropic:
89:    worker: package://provider-anthropic
91:  provider-openai:
92:    worker: package://provider-openai
95:  provider-deepseek:
96:    worker: package://provider-deepseek
98:  provider-xai:
99:    worker: package://provider-xai

## llm-router 1.4.41 provider contract (with evidence)

### Sources used
- **[A] Live engine** ws://127.0.0.1:49160, namespace `bastion`, read-only calls only. `engine::functions::list` hides internal functions. `engine::functions::info function_id=<id>` returns the full `request_schema` and `response_schema`; I found it in the `iii` CLI binary. Saved dumps are in the scratchpad as `i_*.json`.
- **[B] Source** at public `github.com/iii-hq/workers`, tags `llm-router/v1.4.41`, `provider-openrouter/v0.1.16`, `provider-deepseek/v0.1.24`. I sparse-cloned them into the scratchpad (`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tacoda-tacoda-bastion/4fe51ecd-d6cc-423f-a39e-68f5e5b7e45e/scratchpad/`). The key files are `llm-router/README.md` (sections "Provider protocol", "Configuration", "Credentials", "Writing a provider worker"), `llm-router/src/types/{router,events,messages,content}.rs`, `src/channels.rs`, `src/registry/rediscover.rs`, `src/registry/register.rs`, and `provider-openrouter/src/{register,router_client,stream_fn,surface,state,wire/*}.rs`.
- **[C] Binaries.** `strings` on `provider-deepseek-0.1.24` and `llm-router-1.4.41` agree with [A] and [B]. Examples: `provider::<id>::stream`, `provider::deepseek::on_router_ready`, `router::provider::resolve`, `router::provider::register`, `router::models::reconcile`.
- **[D] iii-sdk 0.25.0** in `~/.cargo/registry`, `src/channels.rs`.
- `~/.iii/skills/llm-router` and `provider-*` hold only marker files, so they had no docs. The packages have no manifest beside the binaries. Each repo dir has an `iii.worker.yaml` instead [B].

### 1. Functions a provider registers (`<id>` is the provider id)
| Function | Request | Response | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `provider::<id>::stream` (required) | `ProviderStreamInput` (below) | `{ok: bool}` | Writes frames to `writer_ref`. Returns the ack after the terminal frame. [A][B] |
| `provider::<id>::refresh_models` | `{}`. Unknown fields such as `_caller_worker_id` are ignored. | `{ok: bool, count: uint}` | Fetches the upstream `/models`, then calls `router::models::reconcile`. The router calls it about 2 s after that provider's config slice changes. [A][B README] |
| `provider::<id>::on_router_ready` | `{}` (RouterReadyEvent) | `{ok: bool}` | Metadata `{"internal":true}`. Re-declares the provider and refreshes the catalog. [B register.rs] |
| `provider::<id>::abort` | `{request_id: string}` | `{aborted: bool}` | Metadata internal. `router::abort` fans out to it. `request_id` is the stream input's `resolution_key`. [A][B] |
| Optional: `::count_tokens`, `::embed`, `::transcribe`, `::speak` | | | count_tokens takes `{model, system_prompt?, tools?, messages, thinking_level?, response_format?}` and returns `{model, tokens, estimator}`. [B README] |

There is no separate auth or status function on the provider. The router computes status in `router::provider::list` (`configured`, `available`, `credential_source`, `credential_ref`, `credential_error`).

**`ProviderStreamInput`** [A] `provider::kimi::stream` schema. The openrouter schema is byte-identical.
- Required: `model: string`, `messages: AgentMessage[]`, `writer_ref: {channel_id, access_key, direction: "read"|"write"}`.
- Optional:
  - `system_prompt`
  - `system_sections: [{text, cache_boundary}]`
  - `cache_intent: {surface_digest}`
  - `tools: [{name, description, parameters, label?, execution_mode?}]`
  - `response_format: {type, schema?}`
  - `thinking_level: off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh`
  - `max_output_tokens: u64`
  - `model_meta: Model`
  - `provider_options: any`
  - `session_id`
  - `resolution_key`: the request id, stable across retries.

**Messages** (`AgentMessage`, untagged union, discriminated by `role`):
- `user`: `{role, content: ContentBlock[], timestamp: i64}`
- `assistant`: `{role, content, model, provider, stop_reason, timestamp, usage?, error_kind?, error_message?, native_stop_reason?, warnings?}`
- `function_result`: `{role, function_call_id, function_id, content, details, is_error, timestamp}`
- `custom`

**ContentBlock** (tagged on `type`):
- `text {text}`
- `image {data, mime, attachment_id?}`
- `file {attachment_id, mime, name, size}`
- `thinking {text, signature?}`
- `redacted_thinking {data}`
- `function_call {id, function_id, arguments}`
- `function_result {function_call_id, content, is_error?}`

**Model** (for the catalog):
- Required: `id`, `provider`, `context_window`, `max_output_tokens`.
- Optional: `display_name`, `input_limit`, `pricing {input, output, cache_read, cache_write}`, `supports_tools`, `supports_vision`, `supports_thinking`, `supports_thinking_off`, `supports_xhigh`, `supports_cache`, `supports_structured_output`, `reasoning_efforts`, `thinking_budgets`, `speech`.

### 2. Discovery and registration
The provider declares itself, and the router also finds live providers by function name.
- **Provider declares itself.** The provider calls **`router::provider::register`** at boot and retries with backoff (500 ms, doubling, max 10 s) until it gets an ack. [B register.rs, README]
  - Payload (`ProviderDeclaration`): `{id (required), display_name?, credential_env_var?, credential_optional?, defaults?: {api_url?, max_tokens?, …extra}, config_schema?, supports_model_listing?, default_models?, default_thinking_level?, context_overflow_hint?, models?, worker_id?, icon_svg?, token?}`.
  - Response: `{id, ok, registration_token}`.
  - The provider stores the raw token in `state::set {scope: "<worker-name>", key: "registration_token"}` and sends it as `token` on every later register, resolve, or reconcile call. The router keeps only a sha256 of it. Re-registering an id without the original token is rejected as an anti-takeover guard. [B state.rs, README]
  - Id rule: `[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}`, so no `::`. [B registry/register.rs:24]
- **Re-declare on restart.** The provider calls `register_trigger("router::ready", "provider::<id>::on_router_ready", {})`. [B]
- **Router finds providers by name.** The router also calls `engine::functions::list {prefix:"provider::", include_internal:true}`. It treats each `provider::<id>::on_router_ready` as a live provider and nudges it to re-declare after function registrations change. So registering that function is effectively required. [B registry/rediscover.rs]
- **Dispatch.** The router calls `format!("provider::{id}::stream")`. [C] router string `provider::` / `::stream`
- **Model routing.** The router routes `{model, provider?}` with `router::chat` in this order [B routing.rs]:
  1. An explicit provider.
  2. The unique available catalog owner of the model id. Two or more owners is an "ambiguous" error.
  3. `routing_heuristics`.
  4. `default_provider`.

  Because of rule 2, each host's catalog model ids must be distinct. openrouter prefixes its ids with `openrouter/`.
- **Config entry.** It is a single engine configuration entry with id `llm-router`. The router composes its schema from the declarations. [B README]
  ```json
  {"default_provider":"…","providers":{"<id>":{"api_key":"secret://NAME","api_url":"https://…/chat/completions","max_tokens":8192}},
   "routing_heuristics":[{"pattern":"^gpt-","provider":"openai"}],"settings":{"stream_timeout_ms":600000,"idle_timeout_ms":120000,"retry_max":2,"output_token_max":null}}
  ```
  The default slice schema is `{api_key (writeOnly), api_url, max_tokens}` when `config_schema` is null. A custom `config_schema` must mark any secret-looking field `writeOnly: true`. [B config/schema.rs]
- **Catalog writes.** `router::models::reconcile {provider, models: Model[], token, discovery?}` returns `{provider, count}`. It is the only catalog write path. [A]

### 3. Streaming
- The router creates an engine channel and passes the writer half as `writer_ref`. The provider opens it with **`iii_sdk::channel::ChannelWriter::new(iii.address(), &writer_ref)`**. Each frame is one JSON text message sent with `writer.send_message(&json).await`. The provider calls `writer.close().await` at the end. That API exists in iii-sdk 0.25.0 [D channels.rs:130-185]. llm-router's `open_sink` uses exactly this [B src/channels.rs].
- **Frames.** Each frame is `AssistantMessageEvent`, tagged on `type` (snake_case), and the vocabulary is frozen [B types/events.rs]:
  - `start {partial}`
  - `text_start {partial}`, `text_delta {delta}`, `text_end {partial}`
  - `thinking_start`, `thinking_delta`, `thinking_end` (same shapes as the text frames)
  - `functioncall_start {partial}`, `functioncall_delta {delta, id}`, `functioncall_end {partial}`
  - `usage {usage:{input,output,cache_read,cache_write,reasoning,cost_usd}}`
  - `ping`
  - `stop {stop_reason, error_message?, error_kind?}`
  - Terminal, exactly one and last: `done {message: AssistantMessage}` or `error {error: AssistantMessage}`.
- `partial` and `message` are full `AssistantMessage` snapshots with `provider` set to the provider id. Delta frames carry only `delta`.
- `stop_reason` is one of `end|length|function_call|aborted|error`. `error_kind` is one of `auth_expired|rate_limited|context_overflow|transient|permanent`. The router retries only `rate_limited` and `transient`, and only before the first frame is forwarded. Providers must not retry themselves. [B events.rs, README]
- Send a `ping` at least every 30 s of upstream silence. The router's idle timeout is 120 s by default. [B stream_fn.rs]
- Treat a closed channel as cancellation, and abort the upstream request. [B README]
- **Tool calls.**
  - Outbound: `tools[]` maps to Chat Completions `{"type":"function","function":{name, description, parameters}}`, with names encoded as `::` → `__` (e.g. `agent::trigger` → `agent__trigger`).
  - Inbound: upstream `tool_calls` come back as `function_call {id, function_id: <decoded name>, arguments: <parsed JSON>}` blocks, with `stop_reason: function_call`.
  - History: `function_result` messages map to role `tool` messages. [B wire/tools.rs, wire/messages.rs, provider_scaffold/names.rs]

### 4. Secrets
**The router resolves the secret and passes the key.** The provider never calls `secrets::*`.
- Per request, the provider calls `router::provider::resolve {id, token, begin_discovery?}`. [A][B router_client.rs]
- Response: `{configured, source: config|env|none, credential?: {type:"api_key", key} | {type:"oauth", access_token, …}, api_url?, max_tokens?, credential_source?: config|env|secret|none, credential_ref?, credential_error?, discovery_attempt?}`.
- `api_url` and `max_tokens` come from the slice, else from the declaration's `defaults`.
- The secret's `consumers` must include `llm-router`, not your worker.
- If you get `credential_source: "secret"` with no credential, report `credential_error`. Do not fall back to an env var. [B README "Credentials", "Operational notes"]

### Implications for your worker
- **You cannot reuse the `llm-router` crate.** No llm-router release pins iii-sdk 0.25.0. Tags v1.4.41 and v1.4.42 pin `iii-sdk = "=0.24.6"`, v1.5.x pins `=0.26.0-rc.5`, and the crate is a path dependency inside the monorepo, not on crates.io. The comment in openrouter's Cargo.toml says the provider and router must share one `IIIClient` type. So with iii-sdk 0.25.0 you must hand-write serde types for the JSON above. The wire is version-independent: 0.24.6-built providers run against this 0.25 engine today (kimi, openrouter) [A].
- **One worker can serve several hosts.** For each configured host, register `provider::<host_id>::{stream,refresh_models,on_router_ready,abort}`, call `register` with that id, store one token per id (for example `state` key `registration_token:<id>`), and bind `router::ready` once per handler.
- **Point `api_url` at the full URL.** openrouter and deepseek POST directly to `api_url`, which is the full `/chat/completions` URL (deepseek's binary has `https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions`). The `/models` URL is derived separately.

### Not confirmed
- **No live check of the full flow.** I did not call `register`, `resolve`, or `stream`, because they are token-gated or have side effects.
- **provider-deepseek and provider-xai are not on the engine right now.** Only kimi, openai, openai-codex, and openrouter show up in the `bastion` namespace, so I read deepseek's contract from its source and binary strings only.
- **Two parts I did not read line by line:**
  - the exact derivation of the `/models` URL in openrouter's `discovery.rs`
  - the full SSE state machine (`sse.rs`, about 730 lines)
- **iii.dev docs and context7 were not consulted.** The source repo at the pinned tags answered every question.
- **Version label mismatch.** The `Cargo.toml` at tag `llm-router/v1.4.41` says `version = "1.4.40"`. I treated the tag as authoritative.

  - History: `function_result` messages map to role `tool` messages. [B wire/tools.rs, wire/messages.rs, provider_scaffold/names.rs]

### 4. Secrets
**The router resolves the secret and passes the key.** The provider never calls `secrets::*`.
- Per request, the provider calls `router::provider::resolve {id, token, begin_discovery?}`. [A][B router_client.rs]
- Response: `{configured, source: config|env|none, credential?: {type:"api_key", key} | {type:"oauth", access_token, …}, api_url?, max_tokens?, credential_source?: config|env|secret|none, credential_ref?, credential_error?, discovery_attempt?}`.
- `api_url` and `max_tokens` come from the slice, else from the declaration's `defaults`.
- The secret's `consumers` must include `llm-router`, not your worker.
- If you get `credential_source: "secret"` with no credential, report `credential_error`. Do not fall back to an env var. [B README "Credentials", "Operational notes"]

### Implications for your worker
- **You cannot reuse the `llm-router` crate.** No llm-router release pins iii-sdk 0.25.0. Tags v1.4.41 and v1.4.42 pin `iii-sdk = "=0.24.6"`, v1.5.x pins `=0.26.0-rc.5`, and the crate is a path dependency inside the monorepo, not on crates.io. The comment in openrouter's Cargo.toml says the provider and router must share one `IIIClient` type. So with iii-sdk 0.25.0 you must hand-write serde types for the JSON above. The wire is version-independent: 0.24.6-built providers run against this 0.25 engine today (kimi, openrouter) [A].
- **One worker can serve several hosts.** For each configured host, register `provider::<host_id>::{stream,refresh_models,on_router_ready,abort}`, call `register` with that id, store one token per id (for example `state` key `registration_token:<id>`), and bind `router::ready` once per handler.
- **Point `api_url` at the full URL.** openrouter and deepseek POST directly to `api_url`, which is the full `/chat/completions` URL (deepseek's binary has `https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions`). The `/models` URL is derived separately.

### Not confirmed
- **No live check of the full flow.** I did not call `register`, `resolve`, or `stream`, because they are token-gated or have side effects.
- **provider-deepseek and provider-xai are not on the engine right now.** Only kimi, openai, openai-codex, and openrouter show up in the `bastion` namespace, so I read deepseek's contract from its source and binary strings only.
- **Two parts I did not read line by line:**
  - the exact derivation of the `/models` URL in openrouter's `discovery.rs`
  - the full SSE state machine (`sse.rs`, about 730 lines)
- **iii.dev docs and context7 were not consulted.** The source repo at the pinned tags answered every question.
- **Version label mismatch.** The `Cargo.toml` at tag `llm-router/v1.4.41` says `version = "1.4.40"`. I treated the tag as authoritative.
